name: The Time Machine Class
blurb: A substitute teacher's cardboard time machine works a little too well
title: The Time Machine Class: Funny Skit Script for 5 Students
description: A 5-minute comedy skit script for 5: a substitute teacher takes the class through time in a cardboard box, and someone climbs out. Free to perform.
h1: The Time Machine Class: a 5-Minute Comedy Skit Script for 5 People
logline: A very enthusiastic substitute teacher turns an old banana box into a time machine and drags a bored class through history. The dinosaurs are pretend, the first wheel is square, and then, at the last stop, a baker from six hundred years ago climbs out of the box.
setting: A classroom. Props: a big cardboard box with painted dials and the sign TIME MACHINE, swimming goggles, a bread roll, a phone, a whiteboard marker, an apron and a little flour or chalk dust.

roles.name: Mr. Finch
roles.note: Adult substitute teacher, written as a man; for a woman use Ms. Finch. Huge energy, loves a show, terrible at plans.

roles.name: Nia
roles.note: Student, any gender. Sharp and sceptical, the first to ask the real questions.

roles.name: Omar
roles.note: Student, any gender. Bored and deadpan, until he is crowned a king.

roles.name: Bea
roles.note: Student, any gender. Worried about marks, happy to be the clever inventor.

roles.name: Tobias
roles.note: Any age, any gender. A village baker from six hundred years ago. Amazed by everything, warm and kind.

script.scene: SCENE 1 – A classroom, first lesson of the day

script.action: A large cardboard box stands at the front, painted with dials and a sign: TIME MACHINE. NIA, OMAR and BEA sit at desks. MR. FINCH, a substitute teacher, bursts in wearing swimming goggles.

script.say: Good morning! Your teacher is away, your worksheets are boring, and I have built this.
It's a box.
It is a time machine, Omar.
It says "Bananas" on the side.
It was a banana box. Now it is a time machine. Everyone, hold the desk in front of you. We are going on a school trip through history.
Is this going to be marked?
Everything in life is marked, Bea. Hold on!

script.action: Mr. Finch turns a painted dial. The students hold their desks without enthusiasm.

script.say: Stop number one! Sixty-six million years ago!
Wow. Dinosaurs.
Don't move. A huge one is right behind Omar.

script.action: Omar, bored, turns around. Nothing. Mr. Finch roars quietly behind his hand.

script.say: It's sniffing you. Stay calm. Dinosaurs can smell homework.
I didn't do my homework.
Then you're safe. Next stop!

script.action: Dial. The students hold their desks a bit more willingly.

script.say: The invention of the wheel. A very clever person is about to roll the first wheel in history.
Can I be the clever person?
Bea, I insist.

script.action: Bea stands and pretends to roll something heavy. It stops at once.

script.say: It doesn't roll.
Because the first one was square. Everyone, tell Bea it's a great start.
Great start.
Thank you. I'll keep working on it.
Sir, can we go somewhere with people? Real people?
Excellent request. Final stop! Six hundred years ago. Hold on tight. This one is a long way.

script.action: Mr. Finch turns the dial hard. He makes a long whooshing noise. The students join in, half joking, louder and louder.

script.sfx: A loud bang from inside the box. Everyone stops.

script.action: The box flap slowly opens. TOBIAS climbs out: an old-fashioned baker's apron, flour on the face, holding a bread roll. Tobias stares at the classroom.

script.say: Where is my oven?

script.action: Silence. The students look at Mr. Finch. Mr. Finch looks at the box.

script.say: Sir, who is that?
No idea. But commit to it.
Welcome, traveller! Who are you?
Tobias Crumb, baker of the village by the river. I was putting bread in the oven. Then the oven made a whooshing noise, and now I am in a room full of tiny tables.
Nice acting.
What is acting?

script.action: Tobias notices the ceiling light and points, terrified.

script.say: Your fire is trapped in the ceiling! Who trapped it there?
It's a light.
It does not flicker. Is it angry? Is it sleeping?

script.action: Nia holds up a phone. Tobias leans in, amazed.

script.say: A tiny window! There is a little person inside it!
That's me. It's a camera.
Hello, little Nia. Are you trapped? Blink twice.

script.action: Omar picks up a whiteboard marker and writes on the board. Tobias gasps.

script.say: You write on walls, and nobody punishes you? You must be a king.
I'm in grade eight.
King Omar the Eighth!
Tobias, tell the class. What is life like in your time?
We wake before the sun. We bake. We carry water. In winter, everyone sleeps in one room to stay warm. On holidays we have honey.
That sounds hard.
It is hard. But the bread is good. Here.

script.action: Tobias breaks the roll and gives a piece to each student. They eat, slowly, not sure if this is still a joke.

script.say: And you? You have trapped fire and tiny windows. You must be very happy.

script.action: The students look at each other. Nobody answers straight away.

script.say: Mostly. We complain a lot.
So do we. About the weather, and the price of flour. Some things never change.

script.sfx: A faint whooshing sound from inside the box.

script.say: My oven! It's calling me. Thank you, King Omar. Thank you, little Nia. Thank you, strange man with fish eyes.
Safety goggles.

script.action: Tobias climbs back into the box. The flap closes.
Nobody moves. Then Omar walks up and lifts the flap. Looks inside. Looks inside again.

script.say: It's empty.
Sir, that was your friend. Right? From the drama club?
I thought he was one of yours.

script.action: A long silence. Nia looks down at the bread in her hand.

script.say: Sir. Is this lesson going to be marked?
Yes. Everyone gets full marks. And nobody tells the head teacher.

script.action: They all slowly turn to look at the box. It does not move. Blackout.

ul: Put the box upstage centre with its open side facing away from the audience. Place it in front of a curtain, a door or a big teacher's desk so Tobias can hide behind before the scene and slip out at the end.
Desks face the audience in a row, so the students react toward the front and the box is always in view behind Mr. Finch.
The two bangs can be a book dropped flat on the floor offstage, or one student slapping a desk out of sight.
When Tobias climbs back in, the flap closes and Tobias crawls out of the back into the hiding place. Omar should wait a slow count of three before lifting the flap.
End on the stillness: everyone turns to the box together and holds the look until the lights go out or someone says blackout.
The first half is about the students not caring. Each stop, they join in a little more, so by the whooshing noise they are loud and almost having fun. That growth makes the bang work.
Mr. Finch must never stop believing in the trip, even when it is clearly silly. The goggles stay on until the very end.
Tobias is not a clown. Play real wonder: the light, the phone, the marker are miracles. The sincerity is what makes it funny and a little magical.
The bread moment is the heart. Slow down when Tobias asks if they are happy, and let the silence sit before Nia answers.
Common mistake: winking at the audience after Tobias leaves. Everyone must be truly unsure, especially Mr. Finch.
Send the class to the future instead: a visitor from two hundred years ahead who finds phones and marker pens hilariously old-fashioned.
For a bigger cast, add more stops with one student leading each, or bring a second visitor out of the box who argues with Tobias about bread.
Part-two hook: the next day the regular teacher returns, opens the box, and finds a fresh loaf and a thank-you note inside.

prompts.keyframe: A cheerful substitute teacher in swimming goggles beside a painted cardboard box labelled TIME MACHINE, three bored students at desks, bright classroom morning light, wide shot, cinematic still, 16:9
shots: Medium shot, slow push in on a cardboard box at the front of a classroom as its flap opens and a flour-covered baker in an old apron climbs out, students frozen, magical comedic mood
Close-up of an old-fashioned baker staring in wonder at a phone screen held up by a student, soft classroom light, warm humour
Wide static shot, a student lifts the flap of an empty cardboard box while the class and teacher stare in silence, eerie playful ending

faq.q: How does Tobias disappear from the box on stage?
faq.a: Turn the open side of the box away from the audience and put it in front of a curtain, door or large desk. Tobias crawls in, then out of the back and hides. Omar waits three seconds before lifting the flap to show it empty.

faq.q: Can we use this for a class performance or post a video of it?
faq.a: Yes. The script is free under CC BY 4.0 for performances, competitions and videos, including monetised ones. Credit "Script: cv.cm".

faq.q: We have only four people. Can it still work?
faq.a: Yes. Cut Bea and give the square wheel to Nia, or have one student play Tobias by leaving early with an excuse. With more people, add students who each lead one stop in time.
